selected.rationale: 100% loss on the webapp->Ordering.API synchronous checkout/order-placement call is the most likely way to expose a missing per-request timeout or retry/idempotency: a silent hang or unconfirmed order when Ordering.API becomes unreachable.

Loss on webapp->Basket.API breaks cart read/write at the start of checkout; the cart is core business state and typically lacks a fallback, so this exposes availability loss and client-timeout absence.

Losing Redis connectivity from Basket.API removes all persisted cart state with no evident fallback, directly turning a checkout/cart path into 5xx/hang and exposing the missing resilience around the cart datastore.

The mobile BFF->Ordering.API loss is a second core synchronous order-placement edge; if webapp had a timeout but the mobile aggregator does not, this path reveals the same no-timeout/unbounded-hang weakness in a different client context.

Dropping the basket-api->RabbitMQ publish event (checkout accepted) can cause orders to be silently never created after the user checks out, revealing missing outbox/persistent-retry handling on the event bus.

Loss on webapp->Catalog.API makes the storefront catalog unavailable to all web users; the high-traffic read path often lacks caching/circuit breaker, exposing availability loss and request-timeout gaps.
Loss of the webapp->Identity.API login/token edge blocks authentication; without a client timeout or alternative auth fallback, the web app can hang or fail sign-in during identity service outage.

A delay on the same critical ordering edge tests whether the caller has a bounded timeout: if the synchronous webapp call has no timeout, injected latency propagates unbounded and hangs the checkout to the client deadline, exposing unbounded latency propagation.
